newsitem.title: INDIA: India unveils measures to boost markets.
newsitem.headline: India unveils measures to boost markets.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram Friday unveiled a package of tax relief and other measures aimed at boosting India's stock markets, which suffered after his federal budget in July.
He exempted all investments in mutual funds from capital gains taxation and doubled the amount investors can borrow from banks against shares to one million rupees ($28,570).
Chidambaram also announced a package for the capital market while replying in parliament to a debate on the 1996/97 (April-March) budget.

He said he would discuss other tax proposals next week before a final vote on the budget presented by the centre-left coalition government, which came to power in June after indecisive general elections.

Chidambaram gave a boost to the bond market by permitting foreign institutional investors, who represent pension funds and portfolio investors, to invest all of their funds in debt instruments. To now, they were allowed to invest only 30 percent in debt instruments.
The government raised by 2,000 rupees ($57) to 15,000 ($425) the limit up to which annual income earned by investors in securities specified by the government would be exempt from income tax.
